title: Import
description: Bring pages in from Markdown files, ZIP exports, Word documents, Google documents and PDFs, notebooks from Evernote, rows from a CSV file or Excel workbook, a Trello, Asana or Monday.com board, or Jira issues that stay in sync.
noDestination: There is no page you can add pages to.

pages.help: Markdown files become pages and folders keep their structure. CSV files become databases, and images that pages link to are uploaded.
pages.notion: From Notion: export as “Markdown & CSV” with subpages, and choose the ZIP as it downloaded (split exports work too). Subpages, databases, relations, callouts, toggles and images come along.
pages.obsidian: From Obsidian: choose the vault's folder, or a ZIP of it. Links between notes ([[wikilinks]] too), embedded images and files, and callouts come along.
pages.textbundle: TextBundle and TextPack files (from Bear, Ulysses, iA Writer and other Markdown apps) become a page each, with their pictures and attachments: choose .textpack files, a ZIP of them, or a folder holding .textbundle folders.

docx.help: Each Word document (.docx) becomes a page, with its headings, lists, tables, links, pictures and footnotes. A heading at the very top becomes the page's title; otherwise the file name does.

pdf.help: Each PDF becomes a page made of its text: larger lines become headings, and paragraphs and numbered or bulleted lists come along, also across page breaks. Running headers, footers and page numbers are left out. A heading at the very top becomes the page's title; otherwise the file name does.
pdf.scans: A scanned PDF has no text to read and can't be imported: run text recognition (OCR) on it first, or upload it to a page as a file.
pdf.attach: Also attach each PDF to its page, for its pictures, tables and layout

evernote.help: Each Evernote export (.enex) becomes a database named after the file, with a row per note. Tags, the creation and update times, the author and the source URL become properties, and the note becomes the row's page with its formatting, lists, to-dos, tables, code blocks, pictures and attachments. Encrypted text is left out.
evernote.export: In Evernote, select notes or a notebook and choose Export → ENEX (.enex), then pick the downloaded files. A ZIP of several exports works too.

names.author: Author
names.encrypted: Encrypted text was left out of the import.

onenote.help: Each file becomes a page with its text, headings, lists, tables, links and pictures. A section's file becomes a page named after the section, with a page under it for each of its pages. Any web page saved as a single file (.mht or .mhtml) can be imported too.
onenote.export: In OneNote for Windows, choose File → Export, then Page or Section and Single File Web Page (*.mht), and pick the saved files here. OneNote's Word (.docx) and PDF exports can be imported on the Word and PDF tabs.

confluence.help: Each page of a Confluence space becomes a page, nested as in the space. Headings, lists, tables, code blocks, info panels (as callouts), expand sections (as toggles), task lists, pictures and attached files come along, and links between pages become page mentions.
confluence.export: In Confluence, open the space's settings and choose Export space → HTML, then pick the downloaded ZIP.

csv.choose: Choose a CSV or Excel file
csv.summary: {name}: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}, {columns, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}
csv.name: Name
csv.noDatabases: There is no database you can add rows to.
csv.cantLoad: This database's properties couldn't be loaded.
csv.newOptions: Select values the database doesn't have yet are added as options.

trello.help: In Trello, open the board's menu and choose Print, export and share → Export as JSON, then pick the downloaded file. The board becomes a database with a board view: lists, labels, members, dates, checklists, custom fields, descriptions and comments come along. Archived lists and cards are left out.
trello.attachments: Nothing is downloaded from Trello: linked attachments stay links, and files uploaded to Trello are linked from each card's page.
trello.summary: {name}: {lists, plural, one {# list} other {# lists}}, {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}}
trello.archived: Archived, so left out: {lists, plural, one {# list} other {# lists}} and {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}}.

asana.help: In Asana, open the project's menu and choose Export → CSV (or JSON), then pick the downloaded file. The project becomes a database with a board view by section: completion, assignees, dates, tags, custom fields, notes, subtasks and dependencies come along.
asana.summary: {name}: {groups, plural, one {# section} other {# sections}}, {items, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}}, {subitems, plural, one {# subtask} other {# subtasks}}

monday.help: In Monday.com, open the board's menu and choose Export board to Excel (with updates if you want them), then pick the downloaded file. The board becomes a database with a board view by group: its columns, subitems and updates come along.
monday.summary: {name}: {groups, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}, {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}, {subitems, plural, one {# subitem} other {# subitems}}

jira.help: Connect a Jira Cloud site to get a database of its issues that stays in step: each issue is a row with its key, status, assignee, priority, type, labels, due date and a link back. Changes go one way, from Jira to Leafdesk.
jira.tokenHelp: Create one in your Atlassian account under Security → API tokens. It is kept sealed on the server and only used to read issues.
jira.noProjects: This account can't see any project. Write a JQL query instead.

errors.unauthorized: Jira refused the email address and API token.
errors.forbidden: This Jira account may not search there.
errors.notFound: No Jira Cloud site answered at this address, or the project doesn't exist.
errors.tooManyIssues: The query finds more than {limit} issues. Narrow it down.
errors.unreachable: Jira couldn't be reached. The sync tries again next time.
errors.runAsGone: The person who set the sync up no longer has an account.
errors.accessLost: The person the sync runs as can no longer edit this database.
errors.keyGone: The Key property was deleted or changed type, so issues can't be matched to rows.
errors.failed: The sync failed. It tries again next time.
errors.invalidSite: That isn't an address Leafdesk can reach.
errors.invalidInput: Fill in the email address, the API token and what to sync.
errors.alreadyRunning: A sync is running. Try again in a moment.

githubPulls.help: Get a database of a GitHub repository's pull requests that stays in step: each pull request is a row with its number, state (draft, open, merged or closed), author, assignees, labels, branches, dates and a link back. Changes go one way, from GitHub to Leafdesk. People are matched by the GitHub account they sign in with.
githubPulls.tokenHelp: Needed for private repositories, and it raises GitHub's rate limit. Read access to pull requests is enough. It is kept sealed on the server.

errors.forbidden: The token may not read this repository's pull requests.
errors.notFound: No such repository, or a private one the token doesn't reach.
errors.unreachable: GitHub couldn't be reached, or its rate limit is spent. The sync tries again next time.
errors.runAsGone: The person who set the sync up no longer has an account.
errors.accessLost: The person the sync runs as can no longer edit this database.
errors.keyGone: The Number property was deleted or changed type, so pull requests can't be matched to rows.
errors.failed: The sync failed. It tries again next time.
errors.invalidSite: That isn't an address Leafdesk can reach.
errors.alreadyRunning: A sync is running. Try again in a moment.

board.links: Nothing is downloaded: files and links in the export stay links.
board.comments: {count, plural, one {# comment goes} other {# comments go}} in the rows' pages, under their author and time.
board.types: Check what each column becomes: the export doesn't say what kind a column is, so it was guessed.

warnings.heading: Left out or changed
warnings.invalidValues: {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}} in “{column}” didn't fit the property and were left empty.
warnings.missingFile: “{path}”, linked from “{page}”, wasn't in the upload.
warnings.unresolvedLink: “[[{target}]]” in “{page}” doesn't match a note or file of the upload, so it stays as text.
warnings.encryptedText: “{page}” had encrypted text, which was left out.

fileNotStored.tooLarge: “{path}” is larger than the upload limit and wasn't stored.
fileNotStored.quotaExceeded: “{path}” wasn't stored: the workspace is out of file storage.
fileNotStored.external: “{path}” was left out: the picture is linked from outside the document.
fileNotStored.unsupportedType: “{path}” was left out: pages can't show pictures of this type.

skipped.nestedZip: “{path}” is a ZIP nested too deep and was left out.
skipped.nestedDatabase: “{path}” would be a database inside a database and was left out.
skipped.duplicate: “{path}” was left out: the full version of the same database was imported.
skipped.tooLarge: “{path}” is too large for one page and was left out.
skipped.unused: “{path}” was left out: no page shows it or links to it.
skipped.unsafePath: “{path}” was left out: its path leads outside the ZIP.
skipped.otherSheet: The sheet “{path}” was left out: only one sheet is imported at a time.
skipped.badNote: The note “{path}” can't be read and was left out.
skipped.notEnex: “{path}” was left out: it isn't an Evernote export (.enex).

warnings.tooManyImages: {count, plural, one {# more picture was} other {# more pictures were}} left out: a saved web page keeps at most {limit}.

errors.tooManyFiles: An import can hold at most {limit} files.
errors.tooManyPages: An import can create at most {limit} pages.
errors.tooManyRows: A file can have at most {limit} rows.
errors.tooManyColumns: A file can have at most {limit} columns.
errors.badZip: The ZIP file can't be read.
errors.nothingToImport: There is no Markdown or CSV file to import.
errors.emptyCsv: The file has no header row.
errors.badWorkbook: The Excel file can't be read.
errors.unsupportedWorkbook: Only .xlsx workbooks without a password can be imported. Save the file as an Excel Workbook (.xlsx) without a password and try again.
errors.badDocx: “{name}” can't be read as a Word document. Only .docx files can be imported; save older .doc files as .docx first.
errors.docxTooComplex: “{name}” is too large or complex to import as one page.
errors.badPdf: “{name}” can't be read as a PDF. It may be damaged or protected with a password.
errors.pdfNoText: “{name}” has no text to import: it looks like a scan. Run text recognition (OCR) on it first, or upload it to a page as a file.
errors.pdfTooComplex: “{name}” is too large to import as one page.
errors.badEnex: “{name}” can't be read as an Evernote export. In Evernote, export the notes as ENEX (.enex) and pick that file.
errors.badMhtml: “{name}” can't be read as a single-file web page. In OneNote, export as Single File Web Page (*.mht) and pick that file.
errors.badTrello: The file isn't a Trello board export. In Trello, choose Export as JSON from the board's menu and pick that file.
errors.badAsana: The file isn't an Asana project export. In Asana, choose Export → CSV or JSON from the project's menu and pick that file.
errors.badMonday: The file isn't a Monday.com board export. In Monday.com, choose Export board to Excel from the board's menu and pick that file.
errors.badConfluence: The file isn't a Confluence space exported as HTML. In Confluence, choose Export space → HTML in the space's settings and pick the ZIP it downloads.
errors.badMapping: Choose where at least one column goes, and each property only once.
errors.noAccess: You can't add pages there, or it no longer exists.
errors.notADatabase: Rows can only be added to a database.
errors.badRequest: The import didn't go through. Nothing was changed.

googleDocs.help: Each Google document becomes a page, read through the workspace's Google Drive connection as a Word document would be: headings, lists, tables, links, pictures and footnotes. A heading at the very top becomes the page's title; otherwise the document's name does.
googleDocs.noConnection: There is no Google Drive connection you can import through. An owner adds Google Drive in Settings → Connections; members can use it once an owner ticks “In chat” for its download_file_content tool.
googleDocs.invalidLink: Not a link to a Google document: “{link}”
googleDocs.searchPlaceholder: Words in the title (empty: the latest documents)
googleDocs.linksOnly: Searching isn't allowed through this connection: paste links to the documents.
googleDocs.chosen: {count, plural, one {# document chosen} other {# documents chosen}}
googleDocs.tooMany: Choose at most {limit} documents at a time.

errors.noConnection: That Google Drive connection can't be used. Ask an owner to check it in Settings → Connections.
errors.unreachable: “{name}” could not be reached. Try again later, or ask an owner to check the connection.
errors.signIn: “{name}” needs signing in to Google again: an owner does that in Settings → Connections.
errors.notFound: A document can't be read through “{name}”: check the link, and that the connection's Google account may open it.

web.title: Save from web
web.description: Save a web page as a page: its text, pictures and a link back to it.
web.help: Paste the address of a web page. Its main text is saved without the menus, ads and footers around it, and its pictures are copied into the workspace. A recipe comes first, with its ingredients as a checklist.
web.intoDatabase: As a row of a database

bookmarklet.heading: Save from your browser
bookmarklet.help: Drag this button to your browser's bookmarks bar. On any web page, click it to save that page here; text you selected on it comes along as a quote.

errors.invalidUrl: That isn't a web address. Paste one that starts with http:// or https://.
errors.blocked: This address can't be saved: it points into a private network, or to a port web pages don't use.
errors.unreachable: The page couldn't be reached. Check the address and try again.
errors.timeout: The page took too long to answer. Try again later.
errors.httpError: The site answered with an error: the page may need signing in, or it no longer exists.
errors.notHtml: This address isn't a web page (it may be a file). Upload files to a page instead.
errors.noAccess: You can't add pages there. Pick another place to save to.
errors.badTarget: A web page can be saved under a page or into a database of this workspace.
errors.tooComplex: The page is too large or complex to save as one page.
